coordinates.locator: KM3NeT-It research-infrastructure page; corroborated by the Letter of Intent for KM3NeT 2.0 ('located at 36°16' N 16°06' E at a depth of 3500 m, about 100 km offshore from Porto Palo di Capo Passero, Sicily, Italy')
coordinates.note: Coordinate given to arc-minute precision by both the official KM3NeT-It site page and the 2016 Letter of Intent (design report); precision_m set to 2000 m to reflect that resolution.

depth.note: Sea-floor depth of the ARCA site; corroborated verbatim by the Letter of Intent ('at a depth of 3500 m').
depth.quote: At a depth of about 3500 m

name: KM3NeT-It / ARCA site (Capo Passero)
notes: Distance offshore (~100 km from Portopalo di Capo Passero) is sourced but not modelled as a field in this schema; recorded in summary.technical.
Secondary sources mention that the KM3NeT-It site was formerly used by the NEMO neutrino-telescope prototype project; this was not checked against an official page and is not asserted here.

summary.plain: A patch of Mediterranean seabed about 100 kilometres off the southeastern tip of Sicily, 3500 metres down, where the ARCA neutrino telescope is being built.
summary.technical: KM3NeT-It deep-sea installation site, ~100 km offshore Portopalo di Capo Passero, Sicily, at 36°16'N 16°06'E, 3500 m depth; hosts the KM3NeT/ARCA detector.
